- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1.5x recent high or 10% below true peak.
- In low sentiment (≤0.1) environments, model often underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward historical mean.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model may lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the cycle; apply 1–3% downward correction for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is volatile or erratic, reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
